title: H3012 (125th General Assembly): Firearm and ammunition, unlawful possession by certain persons

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2022-12-08; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess125_2023-2024/prever/3012_20221208.htm (LegiScan doc 2617249))
provenance.note: Introduced text of 2022-12-08; no passage vote. Struck: the 'violent crime ... felony offense' trigger, the old fine/5-year penalty, and subsection (D) wording about violent offenses (replaced). Text quoted as it reads after the bill.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(A)): It is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of a crime punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of five years or more to possess, ship, transport, or receive a firearm or ammunition within this State.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(B)): A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction: (1) for a first offense, must be imprisoned not more than ten years; (2) for a second offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of five years, but not more than thirty years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted; and (3) for a third offense or subsequent offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of fifteen years, but not more than thirty years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(E)): A prior offense for purposes of this section means any conviction related to the possession, shipping, transporting, or receiving of a firearm or ammunition in this State, another state, or in violation of federal law.
